numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In the pre-fix Pallas Triton atomic lowering, min/max on unsigned integers used the signed RMW ops (MIN/MAX) instead of UMIN/UMAX, and floating point min/max was passed straight to the Triton MIN/MAX RMW ops, which the PR says has inconsistent NaN semantics. The passages do not give a concrete wrong output value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Atomic min/max on unsigned integers should use UMIN/UMAX. Floating point min/max should be expanded via integer min/max on bit patterns (atomic_smin/atomic_smax for non-negative values, atomic_umax/atomic_umin otherwise, per the _expand_atomic_fp_min_max docstring), matching np.max / np.min for the tested values.

category_specific_evidence: Atomic min/max lowering for unsigned integers and floating point types was fixed for Pallas Triton on ROCm (PR#26604).

Floating point min/max is expanded via a sequence of integer min/max: atomic_smin/atomic_smax when the value is non-negative, atomic_umax/atomic_umin otherwise (docstring of _expand_atomic_fp_min_max), stated as not handling NaNs.
The test_scalar_atomic parameters for max_f32 and min_f32 were changed from [1,2,3,4] to [-2,-1,0,1] so that negative values are exercised, compared against np.max and np.min.
The ROCm skip for atomic fmin/fmax in the tests was removed, with neutral values -inf for max and +inf for min for float types.
Reviewers noted NaN semantics are inconsistent and unresolved; a docstring was requested describing NaN behaviour; the option of matching np.max/np.maxnum via a CAS loop was raised but not decided.
_fp_bits_type maps float types to signless integer types of the same width, used for bitcasting in the expansion.
reproduction_risks: NaN handling of the expanded float min/max is unspecified in the passages; reproduction should not assume np.max or np.maxnum NaN semantics.
The sign-dependent integer-op expansion relies on the bit-pattern ordering of IEEE floats; negative-value and zero cases are the ones that exercise the umax/umin branch.
Exact expected values for the violated formula and the failing concrete inputs before the fix are not given in the passages.
Tolerance, precision beyond float32 dtype, and magnitude regime are not stated.

provenance.value: Atomic min/max lowering in the Pallas Triton backend used signed-only RMW ops (MIN/MAX) for unsigned integers and floating point values, which the commit message describes as incorrect handling of unsigned integers and float types; floating point min/max was lifted from the Triton frontend with inconsistent NaN semantics
Atomic min/max on unsigned integers should use unsigned RMW ops (UMIN/UMAX), and floating point min/max should be expanded via integer min/max on bit patterns, matching np.max or np.maxnum semantics

In the pre-fix Pallas Triton atomic lowering, min/max on unsigned integers used the signed RMW ops (MIN/MAX) instead of UMIN/UMAX, and floating point min/max was passed straight to the Triton MIN/MAX RMW ops, which the PR says has inconsistent NaN semantics. The passages do not give a concrete wrong output value.

Atomic min/max on unsigned integers should use UMIN/UMAX. Floating point min/max should be expanded via integer min/max on bit patterns (atomic_smin/atomic_smax for non-negative values, atomic_umax/atomic_umin otherwise, per the _expand_atomic_fp_min_max docstring), matching np.max / np.min for the tested values.
